title: onprem-garden-path-weekly-notes-oct-2026
content:
Week window: 2026-10-04 to 2026-10-10
Owner: Asha Raghavan (eng-private-deployments)
Attendees: Asha, Diego, Lin, Priya, Sam (SRE on-call) + CS lead (Maya)
Purpose: weekly triage + standup for the Aperture Labs on-prem install and related VPC networking gotchas

1) Quick status snapshot
- Aperture Labs: in-progress, day 6 of onsite install (remote-run). Core services up but inference nodes flapping under load.
- NetOps: VLAN split policy applied yesterday, awaiting routing confirmation from customer side.
- Package rollout: private-deploy 1.7.2 candidate deployed to control plane; worker nodes still on 1.7.0 in cluster B.

2) Notable incidents this week (short timeline)
- 2026-10-05 09:10 PDT: Observed KV cache thrash causing OOM on node worker-03. Crash loop observed after 30m of sustained 1KB token bursts.
  - Immediate mitigation: reduced max_cache_window to 128MB (from 512MB) on worker-03; node recovered.
  - Root hypothesis: weird sequence-length distribution from customer load (many long prefaces) + a quantized model path edge-case; looking at telemetry.
- 2026-10-06 14:40 PDT: Control plane telemetry missed 3 heartbeats from cluster B for ~18 minutes. Restarted control-plane-agent to re-establish leader election.
  - Suspected cause: MTU mismatch on customer VPN appliance; packet fragmentation of gRPC health streams.

3) Customer-specific blockers (Aperture Labs)
- Blocker A: Persistent inference node flapping under production workload.
  - Evidence: nodes recover on scale-down, fail on scale-up. CPU usage spikes to 96% and then kernel OOM kills some processes.
  - Temporary workaround: capped autoscale to +2 nodes and increased sidecar OOM score to lower priority for RL worker process.
  - Next steps: schedule remote profiling session with Aperture on 2026-10-08 10:00 PDT (Lin owning). Add sampling profiler and get pprof dumps.
- Blocker B: Customer network applies asymmetric routing to egress, causing intermittent gRPC timeouts to S3-compatible object store.
  - Impact: model shards failing to download on cold starts.
  - Workaround: pin model prefetch to control-plane on node boot; staged a prefetch shim that retries with smaller parallelism (PR #287).
  - Ask for customer: provide traceroute+tcpdump during a cold start attempt (Maya to coordinate).

4) Observations / Weirdness (garden-path items)
- Sequence-length distribution mismatch: Aperture's prompt templates include a base64-encoded blob in every request that expands post-tokenization — causes our batching heuristics to under-estimate memory needs. Need to add a pre-tokenization size-checker hook in the ingress layer.
- MTU pathology: when MTU < 1500 on customer VPN, our gRPC keepalive packets get fragmented and reordered on certain vendor appliances. Observed similar symptoms to earlier "heisen-route" incidents but only when combined with TLS session resumption.
- Kernel TLS offload + NVMe driver interactions on worker-03 produced intermittent write stalls — correlates to degraded KV cache persistence.

5) Action items (owners and rough ETA)
- Lin: Run remote profiling on 2026-10-08; capture pprof CPU + heap and upload to PD-4123. ETA: 2026-10-08 EOD.
- Diego: Land a small ingress pre-tokenization size-checker experiment (branch: ingress/max-prefetch-check). Measure false positives on dev cluster. ETA: 2026-10-09.
- Priya: Add MTU diagnostic to install-runbook and include tcpdump commands snippet + expected ICMP behavior. ETA: 2026-10-07.
- SRE (Sam): Create temporary runbook step to set net.core.rmem_max and net.core.wmem_max during installs when MTU<1500; coordinate with CS. ETA: 2026-10-07.
- Maya (CS): Collect customer traceroute + tcpdump during cold-start window and share S3 URL. ETA: 2026-10-08.

6) Meeting notes / decisions
- Decided to avoid forced immediate model rollback; prefer to profile and optimize cache configuration first.
- Agreed to push small control-plane prefetch shim to stabilize cold-starts (hotfix channel). Diego to monitor after merge.
- We will not change autoscale min nodes until after profiling results; autoscale cap remains +2.

7) Risks and escalation paths
- Risk: If KV cache persists to disk fails again under heavy churn, we risk multi-node synchronized cold starts — customer-run SLA impact. Escalation: call SRE lead -> Prepare emergency rollback to quantized-compat model (PD-4119) if pprof shows cache leak.
- Risk: Customer-side MTU quirks could hide a class of intermittent failures across other installs. Plan: add MTU test in preflight and block install if negotiation fails.

8) Runbook updates to capture after this week
- Add pre-tokenization size-check to ingress checklist.
- Document MTU negotiation steps + tcpdump examples.
- Note: add a note about NVMe driver version ranges that surfaced in worker-03 crash (kernel 5.10.x oddities).

9) Quick logs / commands used in mitigation (for handoff)
- Temporarily reduce KV cache on worker-03:
  curl -X POST http://control-plane.local/api/nodes/worker-03/config -d '{"max_cache_window": 134217728}'
- Prefetch shim args used in CANARY: --prefetch-parallelism=2 --retry-backoff=4s
- pprof capture command (Linux):
  go tool pprof -seconds 30 http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/profile

10) Notes to self / open questions
- Q1: Should we add a preflight synthetic cold-start test that fetches a 2GB model shard to validate network/MTU? Pros: catches egress path silently. Cons: costly and slow.
- Q2: Can we detect base64-like payloads pre-tokenization and route them to a special path that estimates token expansion? Prototype idea: rapid token-count estimator using tokenizer-lite (JS).
- Q3: How many other customers use the same VPN vendor as Aperture? If >3, push MTU negotiation into default installer. (Diego to query asset inventory)

11) Next syncs
- Rapid triage: 2026-10-07 09:30 PDT (15m) to review profiling artifacts.
- Weekly install review: 2026-10-11 11:00 PDT (30m) to re-evaluate production rollback/patch plan.

Appendix: quick links
- Jira: PD-4123 (Aperture node flapping)
- Runbook (work-in-progress): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PD/Onprem+install+runbook
- Canary PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy/pull/287

End notes: rough, conversational notes — please tidy before copying to customer-facing handoff.
